title: Komlós conjecture
formal: Does there exist a universal real constant \(C>0\) such that, for all integers \(m,n\ge 1\) and every real matrix \(A\in \mathbb{R} ^{m\times n}\) with \(\sum _{i=1}^{m} A_{ij}^{2}\le 1\) for each column j, there is a vector \(x\in \{- 1,1\}^{n}\) satisfying \(\max _{1\le i\le m}|\sum _{j=1}^{n} A_{ij}x_{j}|\le C\)?
definitions: All matrices are finite. Columns may have arbitrary real entries, including negative entries. The sign vector may depend on the entire matrix; C may not depend on the dimensions or entries. This is an existence question, with no algorithmic or input-encoding requirement.

context_blocks.text: Discrepancy measures how accurately a fractional choice can be replaced by signs while controlling many linear constraints simultaneously. Komlós asks whether normalizing every column in Euclidean norm suffices to bound every coordinate of the signed sum by an absolute constant.

The 2025 improvement gives a polylogarithmic bound smaller than the classical square-root-logarithmic bound, but does not reach a constant. Komlós implies the Beck–Fiala conjecture after scaling an incidence matrix; the converse is not known. Both are retained as established landmarks with different hypotheses, rather than as unrelated questions.

why: A defining vector-balancing conjecture with consequences for rounding, approximation and the geometry of linear constraints.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, preserving the quantifiers, model and guarantees. Conditional results settle only their conditional claims. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.

references.title: Decoupling via Affine Spectral-Independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós Bounds Beyond Banaszczyk

progress.text: The authors improve the general Komlós upper bound to roughly a fourth power of log n, with additional logarithmic factors; a universal constant is not obtained.
